178: dropped without replacement. Each retained task keeps its selected task ID,
179: source revision and task text and is graded by its reviewed validator. Reports
180: disclose the reduced C and Rust strata and the absence of Java.
181: 
182: MultiLang does not publish a separate per-row ingestion timestamp. #50 must prove
183: the semantics and normalization of `created_at` before it becomes the recency key;
184: if that proof fails, the freeze is blocked pending a new owner decision. Applied
185: to the unvalidated pinned inventory, this rule's projected oldest selected value
186: is `2026-04-17T03:18:51Z` (`danielmiessler__Fabric-2098`, Go). The projection is
187: planning evidence, not a frozen task: validation may move the final oldest date
188: earlier while preserving the exact language and repository allocation.
189: 
190: The MultiLang adapter is part of the measuring instrument and must consume each
191: task's declared rebuild/test/print commands, log parser and image. It must discover
192: the repository root rather than assume `/testbed/.git`, safely isolate untrusted
193: parser/test execution, support compiled-language resource needs, pin images by
194: digest and emit typed failures. Existing Python/Inspect scorer evidence does not
195: admit this adapter. #50 records the exact adapter, evaluator and schema versions
196: and fresh validation evidence.
197: 
198: The scheduler creates seeded task/repetition blocks containing exactly all seven
199: arms. It may execute sequentially and may defer a quota-blocked slot within a
200: block, but cannot omit it or begin a later block early.
201: 
202: Stage A runs every block in schedule order from one ledger under one admitted
203: configuration and the owner-approved numerical freeze. Approval of that freeze
204: is the only launch decision. The cohort has no first-block stop and no owner
205: go/no-go between blocks. Each block runs under the admitted per-block
206: supervisor watchdog. After a block completes cleanly, the launcher
207: automatically starts the next block from the same ledger under the same
208: supervisor policy, with no operator action. A block that does not complete
209: cleanly, including a watchdog stop, stops the cohort fail-closed. An uncertain
210: or active attempt is never replayed, the ledger is never reset, and an
211: infrastructure stop retains the ledger and evidence for diagnosis. Resuming
212: the same ledger requires the same admitted configuration and is a recovery,
213: not a new approval.
214: 
215: The Claude arm's enrollment receipt must cover each pending Claude turn under
216: the frozen phase limits. An authenticated renewal during the run is a recorded
217: operator recovery, not an owner decision. It keeps the same account, token,
218: tier and credit/isolation settings and authenticates against the frozen
219: identities. It carries a new recorded account-policy confirmation and adds no
220: reservation or refund. It never extends or overwrites the original receipt,
221: and it is bound into the ledger and evidence. Without a valid renewal, a
222: pending turn the receipt cannot cover fails closed before reservation, and a
223: renewal with a changed identity is rejected.
224: 
225: After every slot is terminal or explicitly unstarted, an offline audit covers
226: all scheduled slots, including every renewal's chronology, before #24 seals
227: the cohort. The historical #155 and #220 first-block executions keep their own
228: stop, audit and owner decisions.
229: 
230: The freeze declares
231: repetitions, the common total workflow deadline, retry policy, concurrency and
232: per-provider/account/local-compute reservations. Stage A freezes exactly one
233: repetition: one trial per arm-task pair, so the schedule has the frozen task
234: count × seven slots (161 for 23 tasks). This directional
235: screen identifies critically failing arms; it does not estimate run-to-run
236: reliability. A study of multiple tries requires a separately identified cohort,
237: predeclared aggregation and interpretation, and results that are not pooled with
238: Stage A.
239: 
240: ## Screening report and futility disposition
241: 
242: Issue #24 seals Stage A independently. Issue #25 publishes all seven arms with
243: scheduled, attempted, valid, unsupported, infrastructure-missing and unstarted
244: denominators; per-task outcomes; all-scheduled lower/upper bounds; task-clustered
245: uncertainty; failure-inclusive time; research/provider/local resource use; and all
246: predeclared paired comparisons. It must say that one task is 1/23 of an arm's
247: denominator, about 4.35 percentage points, and must not present close ordering
248: as a precise ranking. Before publishing
249: the trusted disposition digest, #25 must validate each disposition record against
250: the independently trusted Stage A outcome seal and the sealed outcome records; the
251: Stage B validator authenticates both that published disposition and its referenced
252: source seal, but does not reinterpret the outcome records itself.
253: 
254: No fixed number of arms is dropped. A standard arm is capability-futile only when
255: 
256: `resolved + capability_unknown + unstarted <= 1`
257: 
258: after every one of its 23 scheduled task slots is reconciled. `capability_unknown`
259: includes every slot whose missingness could conceal a resolution. The rule is an
260: absolute resource stop, not statistical proof of general inferiority. An arm with
261: an upper bound of at least 2/23 survives. Failure to achieve frozen admission or
262: minimum valid coverage after the predeclared bounded attempts is reported as
263: `unsupported` and decided separately; it must not be described as capability
264: culling. Every disposition and its inputs are sealed as
265: `stage-a-capability-disposition/1`: one ordered record per scheduled Stage A
266: slot (161), carrying the frozen slot
267: ID, arm ID and one of `resolved`, `not_resolved`, `capability_unknown` or
268: `unstarted`, plus the Stage A freeze, outcome slot-plan and source outcome-seal
269: digests. The same calculation is performed independently for each of the seven
270: arms, including Claude Code; it cannot be omitted from the disposition input or
271: treated as an automatic survivor.
272: 
273: ## Stage B — selected-arm expansion cohort
274: 
275: After the Stage A seal and report, #50 freezes a new corpus containing no Stage A
276: task. Prefer repository-disjointness from Stage A and development/shakedown exposure
277: where feasible, freeze exclusions before outcomes, and disclose unavoidable overlap.
278: The arm set is every surviving standard arm plus `relayview-sol`, `relayview-local`
279: and one standard single-agent Pi baseline under newly frozen exact identities.
280: RelayView production delivery (#64), Intel-successor exact-pair admission (#172), research readiness
281: (#68) and Pi adapter/admission (#130) gate Stage B only. A material configuration change to a
282: standard arm requires a new name and admission; it is not the same continuing arm.
283: 
284: The owner freezes Stage B sample size, language/repository allocation, practical
285: thresholds, repetitions, resources and exact arm set after seeing the complete
286: Stage A report but before any Stage B outcome. Stage A may inform those prospective
287: choices. Stage B task selection may use only frozen metadata and validation, not
288: which Stage A tasks or arms succeeded. The cohort is described as
289: `<N>-arm selected expansion`, with three through ten arms; it is ten-arm only
290: when all seven standard arms survive. Standard Pi must not be silently omitted if
291: admission is unavailable: an altered arm set needs a new explicit owner decision.
292: 
293: Issue #23 schedules the exact frozen Stage B arm set. #24 produces a separate seal.
294: #25 produces a separate expansion report and does not combine numerators,
295: denominators or uncertainty with Stage A. It discloses the selection procedure and
296: limits generalization accordingly. #66 analyzes RelayView's paired checkpoints
297: only from the Stage B seal and supplies that secondary analysis to the expansion
298: report.
299: 
300: ## Standard single-agent Pi
301: 
302: [#129](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/129) pins the
303: [standard single-agent Pi baseline](../authoritative/pi-standard-baseline.md): Pi
304: 0.85.0, `openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol`, ChatGPT OAuth, high reasoning, native prompt
305: and instruction discovery, one RPC-controlled agent, all seven Pi built-in coding
306: and search/list tools, and only the controlled research pair as a non-native
307: extension. [#130](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/130)
308: implements and admits that exact identity. No extra Pi-local arm is implicitly
309: approved.
310: 
311: The capability inventory covers file read/edit/write, text/file search, shell,
312: tests/builds, interruption/deadlines/output bounds, repository instructions,
313: native context handling, provider features and admitted research. Distinguish native
314: tools, necessary benchmark capture/isolation/research adapters, optional commonplace
315: extensions and RelayView-specific enhancements. A practical baseline is not a claim
316: of identical capabilities or an intentionally weakened agent.
317: 
318: Stage B prospectively freezes the existing shared-broker/GitHub-excluded treatment
319: for every selected arm, including Pi and RelayView, with fresh exact-policy admission.
320: Do not reinterpret old native/public-web evidence as admission. One workflow budget
321: covers every role/continuation/retry; reviewer research remains zero under the
322: existing policy. No additional memory/code-intelligence/assistance allowance is
323: introduced.
324: 
325: ## Outcome dimensions and evaluator integrity
326: 
327: The implemented prospective [task outcome v2 contract](task-outcomes-v2.md) versions
328: verifier result, terminal reason, delivery-within-budget, primary task outcome/score
329: and applicable automated/human dispositions separately. The
330: [implemented timeout policy](../authoritative/task-budget-outcomes.md) remains:
331: eligible active-agent deadline timeout is primary zero, terminal and non-retryable.
332: A passing retained patch may separately have verifier pass. Setup/auth/provider/
333: capture/scorer failures and manual cancellation are not invented test failures.
334: Unknown identity/usage remains unknown. Specify combined-cause precedence and
335: eligibility deterministically before execution.
336: 
337: Preserve upstream task/tests/evaluator semantics. #50 validates local integration
338: using repeated gold and base/no-op controls, the same patch through upstream and
339: integrated paths where feasible, correct rebuild instead of stale compiled output,
340: test discovery, setup/parser failures and candidate test tampering. Reuse existing
341: coverage. Supplemental behavioral tests are separately labeled diagnostics, never
342: silent changes to the official score.
343: 
344: Historical logs, seals and original interpretations stay immutable. Any offline
345: reinterpretation identifies both original and successor policy; preserve the
346: disclosed after-observation adoption of the existing timeout policy.
347: 
348: ## Reporting, generalization and resource limits
349: 
350: #25 publishes predeclared paired wins/losses, task-clustered uncertainty,
351: scheduled/attempted/valid/missing denominators, all-scheduled bounds and
352: failure-inclusive latency. Repetitions are not new independent repositories.
353: A 23-task screen changes about 4.35 percentage points per task; zero to four
354: examples per language cannot support language rankings. Recency-first selection is purposive,
355: not random; resampling does not cure that limitation. Dates do not establish
356: absence from pretraining, public mirrors or developer tuning.
357: 
358: Disclose Stage A-informed selection/sizing and Stage B repository/development
359: overlap; describe familiar/new repositories separately when overlap is unavoidable.
360: “No significant difference” does not establish no degradation. Confirmatory
361: non-inferiority requires a predeclared tolerable margin, comparison, uncertainty
362: criterion and adequate sample/resources. Inconclusive results remain publishable.
363: 
364: Freeze actual versus unavailable token/output/turn enforcement, all-role/provider
365: and research usage, workflow deadlines and local CPU/GPU/memory/concurrency limits.
366: Report cold/warm provisioning/cache effects and unknown metrics. Equal wall time
367: is not equal compute; subscription use is neither zero cost nor grounds for
368: inventing a per-task API price. Preserve account counters and reservations.
369: A finite cohort window, bounded operational attempts and resource-stop rules
370: prevent indefinite waiting. Unsupported admission is not capability-futility.
371: The retained upper-bound rule (at most one possible resolution, 1/23) is
372: near-total-failure screening, not a precise inferiority test or economical
373: arm-ranking procedure.
374: 
375: GitHub exclusions block legitimate documentation including GitHub Pages and do not
376: prevent every solution exposure. Retain sanitized denial/filter diagnostics, not
377: blocked source content, and label restricted-source conditions. A realistic-docs
378: sensitivity cohort is optional later work, not a post-results exception.
379: 
380: ## Later feature attribution
381: 
382: [#132](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/132) owns a
383: separate held-out RelayView-only ablation study after the first product baseline,
384: consuming [RelayView #446](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/pi-coding-agent-setup/issues/446).
385: Design may proceed earlier. Use a stripped RelayView control and prioritized
386: feature-specific contrasts as features ship; distinguish incremental from
387: full-minus-one designs and record interactions. Feature-off must remove execution/
388: tool admission and isolate mutable state. Reject impossible combinations or name
389: them as compound interventions; planner removal may alter reviewer snapshots too.
390: 
391: Control task/model routes and total budgets, with comparable extra self-work where
392: feasible for review attribution. Initial/reviewed checkpoints alone measure
393: review-plus-correction, additional work and selection—not a reviewer-only causal
394: effect. Publish regressions and missingness. Hidden scores never guide agents,
395: escalation, retry or candidate choice.
396: 
397: Do not transplant RelayView tools into competitors as a required experiment.
398: No new memory, probe, expert, code-intelligence or ablation delivery delays the
399: first Stage A/B baseline. Governance/recovery/human-review benefits need their own
400: deterministic fault-injection evidence or declared human rubric, not coding scores.
401: 
402: ## Delivery ownership
403: 
404: - #18 tracks the two-stage program and its completion identities.
405: - #23 implements stage-aware, variable-arm-set scheduling and resume checks.
406: - #24 prepares the successor Stage A freeze from #219's adoption record,
407:   executes and seals each cohort separately, and owns Stage A seal accounting.
408: - #25 owns the complete screening report/dispositions and the later expansion
409:   report; screening publication does not wait for #66.
410: - #50 owns the Stage B corpus/resource freeze; its historical Stage A freezes
411:   and MultiLang measurement readiness remain preserved records.
412: - #219 owns the full reviewed archive release and its 23-task adoption record.
413: - #62/#64 own RelayView delivery. Closed #65 is historical v4/VnimanieAI
414:   admission; #172 owns the staged-v5 Intel-successor admission required by Stage B.
415: - #128 owns executable v4 reconciliation, #129/#130 standard Pi specification and
416:   admission, #131 outcome dimensions, and #132 later within-RelayView ablations.
417: - #160 owns the v5 Claude Code identity and seven-arm contract amendment; a
418:   separate fresh delivery/admission record must precede any live Claude task.
419: - #66 owns Stage B RelayView checkpoint analysis only.
420: - #68 and #70–#73 retain historical declared research delivery/admission evidence.
421:   #112–#116 own the GitHub-excluded successor policy, implementation, legacy-six-arm
422:   integration and fresh admission. #98–#102 remain historical public-web
423:   qualification evidence and cannot admit the successor cohort.
424: 
425: The [delivery roadmap](unified-benchmark-roadmap.md) translates these rules into
426: issue-specific acceptance changes. Executable successor schemas, fixtures, adapter and
427: scheduler enforcement must be delivered and tested before a freeze can authorize
428: live trials; v1–v4 validation artifacts must not be relabeled as v5 compliance.

250: ## Conserved Claude subscription accounting

252: `claude-capacity-ledger/1` implements the #167 owner-approved Max 5x assumptions:
253: 3 session percentage points and 1 weekly percentage point per whole attempt,
254: two workflow units held back, concurrency one, no credits or paid overflow,
255: and evaluation-only usage. The historical 12%/2% example yields 29/98 workflow
256: units before the two-unit holdback; it is never a live reading.

258: Observations contain both exposed windows, their epoch IDs and reset times,
259: nonsecret evidence digests, and explicit account/restriction fields. Missing or
260: stale readings, a provider restriction, outside usage, a changed tier, credits,
261: or an unaccounted newly exposed cap reject dispatch. A reading expires after
262: 300 seconds or at the first reset boundary, whichever occurs first. Missing
263: Opus-only telemetry remains the specific owner-accepted exception.

266: rounded percentage cannot replenish spent units. A changed epoch needs a

268: window is rebaselined. Active leases carry a conservative whole-workflow charge
269: into a new epoch; the other window keeps its consumption. Finishing, failing,
270: timing out or restarting a workflow never refunds its charge.

538: #220 Glaze-only freeze schedules seven slots and cannot be resumed to block two.

545: leaves build products out of the candidate and records every outcome
546: in the native report's `capture` record

556: and the final score. Three sequential Tasks run the native workflow, hidden test
557: commands, and isolated parsing/scoring. The hidden scorer returns the existing
558: resolution/status identities as Inspect score metadata. Each evaluation cleans
559: up before the next starts; read-only Docker inspection proves quiescence. The
560: image store retains only admission, image ownership, locks and resource policy.

562: in place, blocking dispatch or image release. The sequential design keeps the
563: 28-GiB task and 2-GiB controller within the declared 30-GiB allocation; the parser does not add its memory ceiling to that peak.

488: ## Portable preparation order
489: 
490: Each step consumes the previous step's output, so run them in this order. Steps
491: marked **owner** need the owner at the host's terminal (masked vault prompts or
492: an attestation); an agent never types into those prompts and never writes an
493: owner record. No step before the launch in step 13 starts a comparative attempt.
494: 
495: 0. Refresh the ChatGPT login (**owner**), then re-admit the execution host at
496:    the final commit. When the cohort moves to another host (attempt 7: asrock
497:    to Alexander), first move the shared-research ledger and its allocation
498:    receipt with the [ledger transfer runbook](research-ledger-transfer.md),
499:    and once the new host is admitted, retire any earlier Stage A ledger it
500:    still holds ([below](#retire-an-earlier-ledger-on-a-newly-used-host-owner-decision)).
501: 1. The archive allowance ([above](#research-allowance)) and its top-up
502:    ([above](#research-allowance-top-up-4)) are already applied; they travel
503:    with the ledger.
504: 2. Export the credential leases to tmpfs (**owner**): the Brave key and every
505:    provider credential, in one vault unlock.
506: 3. Fresh research and provider admission: the read-only remainder pre-check,
507:    deployment, Claude enrollment and quota (**owner**), Claude admission, the
508:    six other arms.
509: 4. Build the plan: configuration, source arm proposal and planning values.
510: 5. Rebind it to the fresh admission.
511: 6. Qualify the release images with the final configuration.
512: 7. Exercise task-input retention.
513: 8. Assemble the unsigned candidate.
514: 9. Owner approval of the exact candidate (**owner**).
515: 10. Publish the approved freeze, once `frozen_at` has passed.
516: 11. Initialize the scheduler ledger.
517: 12. Renew the Claude enrollment for the cohort window (**owner**).
518: 13. [Launch preflight](#pre-launch-checks) once the window opens, then
519:     [`systemd-run`](#launch).
520: 
521: Merge nothing to `main` from step 0 until the launch. Host admission, Claude
522: admission (step 3) and the plan build (step 4) fetch `origin/main`, so they
523: need Gitea to answer, and they refuse with `source branch moved from selected
524: commit` once `main` has moved past the admitted commit. After a merge in that
525: window, steps 3 and 4 can no longer run or be rerun at the admitted commit;
526: recover by re-admitting at the new commit (step 0).
527: After the launch, merges never block the cohort or a reboot recovery
528: ([below](#keep-the-host-unchanged-while-the-cohort-runs)).
529: 
530: The provider-free [systemd rehearsal](#required-systemd-rehearsal) has no
531: inputs from these steps; complete it before step 9, since its result is part
532: of what the owner approves.
533: 
534: Image qualification must follow the rebind: the archive candidate accepts only
535: a fresh `stage-a-image-qualification/1` whose `configuration_digest` is the
536: digest of the final, rebound configuration, and rebinding changes that digest.
537: Fresh research admission must follow the top-up, because new setups take
538: their account limits from the newest allocation journal and admission requires
539: them to equal the frozen capacity.
540: 
541: **Timing.** Four clocks bound the preparation:
542: 
543: - The research deployment of step 3 sets a 6-hour deadline
544:   (`--duration-seconds 21600`): the Claude admission's research probe and the
545:   six other arms' probes must all complete within 6 hours of preparing it.
546: - The fresh admissions are valid for 35 days less five minutes from step 3.
547:   The cohort window that step 8 assembles is `review_hours` (6 hours) of owner
548:   review, one hour to the start, then the 161-slot budget (2,526,909 s, about
549:   29.25 days) plus one day: about 30.5 days from assembly. Steps 3 to 8
550:   therefore have about 4.4 days; step 8 stops if the window would outlast the
551:   admissions.
552: - The owner approves within those 6 review hours: an approval recorded after
553:   `frozen_at` is stale and is refused. Publication then waits until
554:   `frozen_at` has passed, and the launch until the window has started.
555: - The Claude enrollment receipt recorded in step 3 is valid for 24 hours and
556:   must still be valid for the Claude admission right after it. Step 12's
557:   confirmation then covers the whole approved cohort window (at most 35 days;
558:   owner decision, 2026-10-06), so the owner does not renew during the cohort.
559: - The ChatGPT login refreshed in step 0 yields a refresh-disabled access token
560:   that lasts 10 days. The preparation and the cohort must finish within it:
561:   the launcher stops before any GPT slot whose token would expire within the
562:   attempt, with nothing reserved.
563:

705:   Meta keys and the Codex ChatGPT login) and a manifest binding each file's

708: The helper exports both from this host's own vault (the registry entry's
709: vault, pinned to the admitted profile's vault digest) in one masked unlock,
710: mode `0600` in a `0700` per-user directory. A reboot removes them: re-export

1: # Continuous Stage A cohort
2: 
3: This runbook operates an `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` freeze: every block of the
4: reviewed archive cohort runs in schedule order from one ledger, under one
5: admitted configuration and one owner-approved numerical freeze
6: ([ADR-0016](../authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md)).
7: For the release `stage-a-prepared-23-v1`, the 23 reviewed tasks with a
8: prepared environment each
9: ([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)),
10: that is 23 tasks × 7 arms = 161 slots. Approval of that freeze is the only launch decision. There is no
11: first-block stop, no `first_block_task_id`, no first-block audit and no owner
12: go/no-go between blocks.
13: 
14: This runbook grants no approval. It prepares the cohort on the portable
15: execution host (`cachyos-alexander` from attempt 7; `cachyos-asrock` before),
16: in the order the tools require, up to the
17: owner's approval of the exact freeze, then publishes, initializes and launches
18: it. The one-task first block keeps its own
19: [runbook](stage-a-first-block-gate.md).
20: 
21: ## What the harness enforces
22: 
23: - **Corpus and scope.** The freeze binds the release identity, the adoption
24:   record's ordered task IDs and its digest. Every count (slots, attempts,
25:   disposition records, host preflight size) derives from the frozen corpus.
26: - **Per-block supervision.** `scripts/run_stage_a.py` runs at most one block
27:   per invocation under the unchanged per-block `SUPERVISOR_POLICY`. After a
28:   clean block (every slot terminal or explicitly unstarted, no reservation) it
29:   appends a chained record under `$artifacts/cohort-progress/` and exits `0`
30:   while blocks remain, or `3` when the cohort is complete. Any other result, an
31:   exception or a watchdog stop exits otherwise and writes no record.
32: - **Crash recovery.** If the process dies after a block settles but before its
33:   progress record is written, the next invocation writes that record from the
34:   ledger first (`caught_up=true`), so later blocks keep their indices. A
35:   completed block must be the next unrecorded block in schedule order. The
36:   launcher reads the ledger under its lock and fails at once if another
37:   launcher holds it.
38: - **No reset.** Each record binds the previous record and every settled slot.
39:   An invocation whose ledger lost or changed a settled slot, or whose record
40:   chain is broken, stops before any work. An active or uncertain reservation
41:   stops the block (`unreconciled active attempt; retain evidence, do not
42:   rerun`). Nothing replays, refunds or reinitializes.
43: - **Unattended credentials.** The unit has no terminal and never unlocks the
44:   vault. Every provider credential comes from the provider credential lease
45:   that step 2 exports with the Brave key: private files on the `/dev/shm`
46:   tmpfs, bound to the admitted vault's digest. A refresh-disabled ChatGPT
47:   token must outlive the slot's admission and native phase (4,020 s).
48: - **Slot rehearsal before reservation.** Before reserving each slot, the
49:   launcher runs that slot's native preparation up to the provider-contact
50:   boundary with nothing reserved: credential delivery from the lease and its
51:   token lifetime, Claude's token against the covering receipt, the research
52:   service start and stop, and the sandbox and observer definition, all torn
53:   down before the credential-holding Inspect evaluation would start. A failure
54:   stops the cohort with the slot still pending, so a resume runs it; only work
55:   past the boundary can leave an uncertain attempt.
56: - **Claude enrollment per turn.** Block entry does not require one receipt to
57:   cover a later Claude turn (a seventh Claude turn needs 95,400 s, more than
58:   a 24-hour receipt). Inside the scheduler lock, immediately before reserving
59:   a Claude slot, the launcher uses the latest receipt (the configured one or a
60:   recorded renewal) already observed and covering Claude admission plus its
61:   native phase (4,020 s) from the current time. Otherwise the cohort stops
62:   before reservation. Serial
63:   owner-managed dispatch (`provider_capacity_mode=owner_managed`, concurrency 1)
64:   makes the checked slot the one reserved.
65: - **Research allowance.** The freeze's numerical policy must select the
66:   archive research allowance `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT` (3,060 calls) or its
67:   top-up `STAGE_A_ARCHIVE_ACCOUNT_2`, which no other scope accepts
68:   ([allowance](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-amendment-251-20261004.md),
69:   [top-up](../evidence/stage-a-archive-capacity-top-up-267-20261006.md)), and
70:   admission requires it to be the identity of the live allocation journal.
71:   Every dispatch, the launch preflight, the cohort audit and the seal require
72:   the live shared remainder (`identity − used − active account reservations`)
73:   to cover, in every dimension, one whole workflow allowance for each attempt
74:   of an unsettled slot that has not finished. Finished attempts are already
75:   charged; the lone in-flight attempt of a slot is credited with its own
76:   `trial-work` charges. Otherwise they stop before any reservation
77:   (`live research remainder cannot cover N whole workflows (<dimensions>);
78:   never borrow`). The check applies to every Stage A scope, so a historical
79:   freeze whose unsettled slots the live ledger can no longer cover is refused
80:   as well. Nothing borrows from another allowance.
81: - **Task-input store.** Archive views and verifier workspaces live in
82:   `${artifacts}.task-inputs`
83:   ([task-input retention](stage-a-first-block-gate.md#task-input-retention)).
84:   The cohort audit requires the store; there is no in-root fallback.
85: - **Unprivileged agents.** Every arm's native agent runs as the agent user
86:   `agent`, with the operator's UID and GID, in dispatch, research admission,
87:   Claude admission and image qualification alike
88:   ([ADR-0026](../authoritative/adr/0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md)).
89:   Run every command in this runbook as the unprivileged operator: the harness
90:   refuses to run as root. The agent owns its sanitized workspace and its arm's
91:   home and holds no capabilities. Inspect's sandbox-tools server stays root,
92:   with its state on a root-only tmpfs at `/run/sandbox-tools`, so the agent
93:   can neither signal it nor remove its state. Sanitization, capture, export
94:   and the verifier run as root. Image qualification builds each task as the
95:   agent and records the build's exit statuses, the user and the workspace
96:   handover's duration (`agent_user.handover_seconds`) in each task's record.
97:   `agent_user.shared_uid_accounts` and `shared_gid_groups` name any image
98:   account that has the operator's UID or GID; the agent still resolves to
99:   `agent`, ahead of them.
100:   An admission or image qualification made before this model does not cover
101:   it: re-admit and requalify at the new commit, then rebind and freeze.
102: - **Prepared environments.** Each task's agent works in its prepared
103:   environment, an owned image derived from its grader's, with its dependencies
104:   installed for offline use; its grader keeps the image its validator names
105:   ([ADR-0029](../authoritative/adr/0029-run-agents-in-prepared-environments-keeping-declared-dependency-paths.md)).
106:   Image preparation loads both images for the block. Sanitization keeps
107:   exactly the task's declared dependency paths (such as `node_modules`), each
108:   checked against its recorded hash, and no capture or export includes one.
109:   Image qualification requires the task's build to exit 0 offline as the agent
110:   within 600 seconds, or stops naming the task unsuitable
111:   ([ADR-0030](../authoritative/adr/0030-require-each-tasks-build-to-succeed-offline-in-time.md)).
112:   The prepared images live in the owner OCI store with the grader images; the
113:   execution host's store must hold both (bootstrap's `oci-store` step).
114: 
115: ## Paths and shell
116: 
117: Everything except the allowance steps below runs **on the execution host**,
118: in one zsh (or bash) shell, from the admitted staged checkout `$base/checkout`: the host must
119: have been re-admitted at the commit that contains this runbook's tools
120: ([portable host, sections 7 to 9](portable-execution-host.md#7-qualify-the-host)),
121: because every launch input binds the admitted profile's commit. From attempt 7
122: the execution host is `cachyos-alexander` (`alexander-evals`, battery-backed,
123: on the dedicated eval daemon); attempts 3 to 6 ran on `cachyos-asrock`,
124: and the allowance steps were applied there. `host_id` and `vault` come from the
125: registry entry this machine verifies as. The operator
126: checkout `~/evals/agent-harness-evals` is used only where a section says so.
127: The launcher requires the admitted profile's paths: the ledger is
128: `state/stage-a/scheduler.json` and the artifact root `artifacts/stage-a/live`
129: under the staged-execution root. Any other ledger or artifact path is refused
130: (`launcher must use the admitted target-local ledger and artifact paths`).
131: 
132: Start every session with these assignments. They change nothing; rerun them in
133: a new shell and continue where you stopped. `attempt` names one private
134: working directory for this cohort's plan, evidence and gate; a refused or
135: abandoned attempt keeps its directory and the next one uses `attempt=2`. An
136: attempt whose cohort launched and stopped is first
137: [retired](#retire-a-stopped-attempt-owner-decision), which moves its ledger and
138: artifact root into its own directory.
139: 
140: ```sh
141: umask 077
142: attempt=1
143: release=stage-a-prepared-23-v1
144: base="$HOME/.local/share/agent-harness-evals/staged-execution"
145: export PATH="$base/runtime/node-v22.19.0-linux-x64/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
146: checkout="$base/checkout"
147: cd "$checkout"
148: commit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
149: profile="$base/artifacts/stage-a/qualification-$commit/host-profile.admitted.json"
150: adoption="$checkout/docs/releases/$release.json"
151: archive_root="$base/archive/$release"
152: research_state="$base/state/shared-research-165"
153: allocation="$base/allocations/archive-top-up-267-attempt-1/receipt/allocation-receipt.json"
154: host_id=$(.venv/bin/python -B -c 'from agent_harness_evals import host_registry; print(host_registry.required_current().host_id)')
155: vault=$(.venv/bin/python -B -c 'from agent_harness_evals import host_registry; print(host_registry.required_current().vault_path)')
156: vault_sha256=$(.venv/bin/python -B -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["paths"]["database_sha256"])' "$profile")
157: lease=$(.venv/bin/python -B scripts/export_stage_a_research_lease.py --print-path)
158: ledger="$base/state/stage-a/scheduler.json"
159: artifacts="$base/artifacts/stage-a/live"
160: cohort="$base/state/stage-a/cohort-$release-attempt-$attempt"
161: deployment="$cohort/research-deployment"
162: matrix="$cohort/research-admission/matrix"
163: claude_admission="$cohort/claude-admission"
164: build="$cohort/build"
165: plan="$cohort/plan"
166: gate="$cohort/gate"
167: configuration="$plan/execution-configuration.json"
168: freeze="$gate/freeze.json"
169: admission="$gate/admission"
170: approval="$gate/freeze-approval.json"
171: ```
172: 
173: `allocation` names the receipt of the archive allowance top-up applied below,
174: the live allocation journal; if that top-up used another `attempt`, change the
175: number in its path. Then enter
176: the admitted profile digest you saved off host at admission, and check it and
177: the profile's paths:
178: 
179: ```sh
180: printf 'Admitted host profile digest saved off host: '
181: read -r trusted_host_digest
182: .venv/bin/python -B - "$profile" "$trusted_host_digest" "$ledger" "$artifacts" "$commit" "$host_id" <<'PY'
183: import json, sys
184: from pathlib import Path
185: from agent_harness_evals.host_profile import reference
186: profile, _ = reference(Path(sys.argv[1]), sys.argv[2])
187: contract = json.loads((Path(profile['qualification_root']) / 'contract.json').read_text())
188: assert profile['status'] == 'admitted' and profile['host_id'] == sys.argv[6], 'admitted profile of this host required'
189: assert profile['paths']['ledger'] == sys.argv[3] and profile['paths']['artifacts'] == sys.argv[4], 'profile paths differ'
190: assert contract['checkout']['commit'] == sys.argv[5], 'staged checkout is not the admitted commit'
191: print('admitted profile', sys.argv[2], 'ledger', sys.argv[3])
192: PY
193: test -z "$(git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all)" && echo 'staged checkout clean'
194: test -d "$artifacts" && test ! -L "$artifacts" && echo 'artifact root present'
195: test ! -e "$ledger" && echo 'no scheduler ledger yet'
196: mkdir -m 700 "$cohort" && echo "attempt directory $cohort"
197: ```
198: 
199: Expected: `admitted profile sha256:… ledger …/state/stage-a/scheduler.json`,
200: then the four confirmations. A digest mismatch, another host, a dirty
201: checkout or a commit other than the admitted one is a stop: requalify instead
202: of editing the profile. Before step 12, an existing ledger means a cohort was
203: already initialized: resume it (below), never reinitialize; from step 12 on the
204: ledger exists and that line prints nothing. An existing attempt directory
205: means that attempt started: continue it, ignoring the `mkdir` refusal, or use
206: the next `attempt`.
207: 
208: The admitted profile must come from a session prepared for the cohort's size
209: (`--preflight-task-count 23`, as the portable procedure does). Host admission
210: derives the expected receipt counts from the payload's synthetic manifest, and
211: every cohort dispatch requires the admitted receipt's `scheduled_slots` and
212: `attempt_count` to equal the frozen schedule (161 and 161). A 175-slot
213: historical receipt cannot dispatch the cohort.
214: 
215: ### Research ledger location
216: 
217: The configuration's `research_state` must equal the allocation receipt's
218: `state_directory`, and dispatch reads the allocation journal from that
219: directory on the host that runs the cohort. When the cohort runs on a host

488: ## Portable preparation order
489: 
490: Each step consumes the previous step's output, so run them in this order. Steps
491: marked **owner** need the owner at the host's terminal (masked vault prompts or
492: an attestation); an agent never types into those prompts and never writes an
493: owner record. No step before the launch in step 13 starts a comparative attempt.
494: 
495: 0. Refresh the ChatGPT login (**owner**), then re-admit the execution host at
496:    the final commit. When the cohort moves to another host (attempt 7: asrock
497:    to Alexander), first move the shared-research ledger and its allocation
498:    receipt with the [ledger transfer runbook](research-ledger-transfer.md),
499:    and once the new host is admitted, retire any earlier Stage A ledger it
500:    still holds ([below](#retire-an-earlier-ledger-on-a-newly-used-host-owner-decision)).
501: 1. The archive allowance ([above](#research-allowance)) and its top-up
502:    ([above](#research-allowance-top-up-4)) are already applied; they travel
503:    with the ledger.
504: 2. Export the credential leases to tmpfs (**owner**): the Brave key and every
505:    provider credential, in one vault unlock.
506: 3. Fresh research and provider admission: the read-only remainder pre-check,
507:    deployment, Claude enrollment and quota (**owner**), Claude admission, the
508:    six other arms.
509: 4. Build the plan: configuration, source arm proposal and planning values.
510: 5. Rebind it to the fresh admission.
511: 6. Qualify the release images with the final configuration.
512: 7. Exercise task-input retention.
513: 8. Assemble the unsigned candidate.
514: 9. Owner approval of the exact candidate (**owner**).
515: 10. Publish the approved freeze, once `frozen_at` has passed.
516: 11. Initialize the scheduler ledger.
517: 12. Renew the Claude enrollment for the cohort window (**owner**).
518: 13. [Launch preflight](#pre-launch-checks) once the window opens, then
519:     [`systemd-run`](#launch).
520: 
521: Merge nothing to `main` from step 0 until the launch. Host admission, Claude
522: admission (step 3) and the plan build (step 4) fetch `origin/main`, so they
523: need Gitea to answer, and they refuse with `source branch moved from selected
524: commit` once `main` has moved past the admitted commit. After a merge in that
525: window, steps 3 and 4 can no longer run or be rerun at the admitted commit;
526: recover by re-admitting at the new commit (step 0).
527: After the launch, merges never block the cohort or a reboot recovery
528: ([below](#keep-the-host-unchanged-while-the-cohort-runs)).
529: 
530: The provider-free [systemd rehearsal](#required-systemd-rehearsal) has no
531: inputs from these steps; complete it before step 9, since its result is part
532: of what the owner approves.
533: 
534: Image qualification must follow the rebind: the archive candidate accepts only
535: a fresh `stage-a-image-qualification/1` whose `configuration_digest` is the
536: digest of the final, rebound configuration, and rebinding changes that digest.
537: Fresh research admission must follow the top-up, because new setups take
538: their account limits from the newest allocation journal and admission requires
539: them to equal the frozen capacity.
540: 
541: **Timing.** Four clocks bound the preparation:
542: 
543: - The research deployment of step 3 sets a 6-hour deadline
544:   (`--duration-seconds 21600`): the Claude admission's research probe and the
545:   six other arms' probes must all complete within 6 hours of preparing it.
546: - The fresh admissions are valid for 35 days less five minutes from step 3.
547:   The cohort window that step 8 assembles is `review_hours` (6 hours) of owner
548:   review, one hour to the start, then the 161-slot budget (2,526,909 s, about
549:   29.25 days) plus one day: about 30.5 days from assembly. Steps 3 to 8
550:   therefore have about 4.4 days; step 8 stops if the window would outlast the
551:   admissions.
552: - The owner approves within those 6 review hours: an approval recorded after
553:   `frozen_at` is stale and is refused. Publication then waits until
554:   `frozen_at` has passed, and the launch until the window has started.
555: - The Claude enrollment receipt recorded in step 3 is valid for 24 hours and
556:   must still be valid for the Claude admission right after it. Step 12's
557:   confirmation then covers the whole approved cohort window (at most 35 days;
558:   owner decision, 2026-10-06), so the owner does not renew during the cohort.
559: - The ChatGPT login refreshed in step 0 yields a refresh-disabled access token
560:   that lasts 10 days. The preparation and the cohort must finish within it:
561:   the launcher stops before any GPT slot whose token would expire within the
562:   attempt, with nothing reserved.
563:

170: retains one task image, executes at most the current seven-slot block, releases
171: the image, and exits with JSON containing `status=block_complete` and
172: `first_block_gate=true`. It cannot select block two in this invocation.
173: 
174: An SSH disconnect does not stop or restart the service. Reconnect and re-enter
175: the same process and ledger through status and journal inspection:
176: 
177: ```sh
178: systemctl --user show "$unit" -p MainPID -p ActiveState -p SubState -p Result -p ExecMainStatus
179: journalctl --user -u "$unit" --no-pager
180: ```
181: 
182: While `MainPID` is nonzero, only observe it; never start another runner. Success
183: requires `MainPID=0`, `SubState=exited`, `Result=success`, and `ExecMainStatus=0`.
184: On failure, retain the ledger, unit journal, attempt directory, image state, and
185: all reservations. Do not rerun: an uncertain or active attempt is intentionally
186: non-replayable.
187: 
188: ## Offline audit and stop
189: 
190: After retaining the successful launch journal, stop the exited service and run
191: the audit in a fresh invocation of the same admitted supervisor unit:
192: 
193: ```sh
194: systemctl --user stop "$unit"
195: systemd-run --user --service-type=exec --remain-after-exit --unit="$unit" \
196:   --property=UMask=0077 --property=KillMode=control-group --property=Restart=no \
197:   --property="CPUQuota=${cpu}%" --property="MemoryMax=$memory" \
198:   --property="TasksMax=$tasks" --property="RuntimeMaxSec=$runtime_seconds" \
199:   --property=Nice=10 --working-directory="$checkout" \
200:   /usr/bin/env -i "PATH=$runtime_path" LANG=C.UTF-8 \
201:   "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u)" \
202:   "$checkout/.venv/bin/python" -B "$checkout/scripts/audit_stage_a_first_block.py" audit \
203:   --freeze "$freeze" --configuration "$configuration" --ledger "$ledger" \
204:   --admission-directory "$admission" --approval "$approval" \
205:   --host-profile "$profile" --trusted-host-digest "$trusted_host_digest" \
206:   --artifacts "$artifacts"
207: 
208: systemctl --user show "$unit" -p MainPID -p SubState -p Result -p ExecMainStatus
209: journalctl --user -u "$unit" --no-pager
210: ```
211: 
212: Expected: the audit exits successfully and immutably writes
213: `$artifacts/first-block-audit.json`. The receipt binds the clean execution commit,
214: host/profile, final freeze, seven-arm index, target admission and owner approval,
215: runtime inventory, resource limits, canonical paths, complete scheduler
216: checkpoint, account reservation history, one task-outcome-v2 record for every attempted slot,
217: exact typed unstarted dispositions, every retained artifact hash, secret scan,
218: hidden-score isolation, and quiescent reservations, images, containers, and
219: volumes. An archive-bound root also passes the task-input retention check
220: described below. Running the same audit again against the unchanged checkpoint
221: reproduces the identical receipt. Any changed input or history is rejected.
222: 
223: Scheduler `started_at` records the reservation before admission checks. Launch
224: intent `started_at` records the later write immediately before native execution.
225: The auditor compares timezone-aware instants and requires reservation time ≤
226: intent time ≤ scheduler completion time. These are distinct events; their text
227: and instants need not be equal. Both original timestamps remain in the retained
228: evidence. An intent outside the reserved interval, or a missing, malformed or
229: timezone-free timestamp, is rejected.
230: 
231: An owner may explicitly resume a held Claude reservation rejected because its
232: account-policy receipt expired **before native execution started**. This narrow
233: recovery keeps the original intent and interruption untouched, with no native
234: artifacts, no additional reservation, and no refund. A new sibling directory
235: `<lease-id>-prelaunch-resume-r1` holds the first native execution. The canonical
236: artifact root retains `prelaunch-recovery-<lease-id>.json`, binding both directory
237: identities, the original inventory, interruption, freeze, configuration and clean
238: execution revision. It also retains the explicit restart decision and new owner
239: account-policy confirmation; the renewed enrollment must keep the same account,
240: token, tier and credit/isolation settings. The original receipt is not extended
241: or overwritten. The audit checks the chronology and both intents against the
242: single reservation, and includes the complete recovery record in the disposition.
243: Any prior native evidence, changed history, missing confirmation or unbound
244: recovery record rejects this path. This is an explicit operator recovery, not an
245: automatic replay feature; it does not authorize later blocks.
246: 
247: Stop after audit even when it passes:
248: 
249: ```sh
250: systemctl --user stop "$unit"
251: ```
252: 
253: No audit failure authorizes continuation. Preserve the failed unit and evidence,
254: diagnose the specific mismatch, and obtain an explicit owner disposition. Deleting
255: the ledger, moving to another artifact directory, or initializing a replacement
256: cohort cannot pass because the admitted profile and freeze bind the original
257: canonical paths and identities.
258: 
259: ## Task-input retention
260: 
261: The audit and seal hash and secret-scan every regular file under the canonical
262: artifact root `$artifacts` with the unchanged `security.SECRET_PATTERNS`. Pinned
263: task sources can legitimately contain credential-shaped examples, so
264: archive-bound execution never writes task-source-derived trees there. The
265: launcher and grader create them directly in the sibling task-input store
266: `${artifacts}.task-inputs`, at the same relative path they would otherwise have
267: had under `$artifacts`. Nothing is moved after the fact, and the scanner is
268: neither weakened nor allow-listed.
269: 
270: | Tree | Created by | Store path |
271: | --- | --- | --- |
272: | Block agent and grader views | launcher, once per block | `archive-inputs-<uuid>/{agent,grader}` |
273: | Grading agent and grader views | grader, once per attempt | `<lease-id>/verification/grade/{agent,grader}` |
274: | Composed verifier workspace | grader, once per attempt | `<lease-id>/verification/grade/verifier-workspace` |
275: 
276: Before creating any tree, each export writes a canonical export record,
277: `task-input-export.json` (`task-input-export/1`), in its canonical directory
278: (`archive-inputs-<uuid>/` or `<lease-id>/verification/grade/`). It names every
279: relocation manifest the export will produce. If the export raises, every
280: planned tree that has no manifest yet is removed from the store, and the record
281: is rewritten to list those names under `removed` with the error type under
282: `failure`. Trees recorded before the failure, for example the views of an
283: attempt whose owned-image grading later fails, are retained and verified.
284: 
285: The retained verifier workspace is exactly the composed effective tree. Its Git
286: metadata is grading scaffolding and is removed before the tree is recorded.
287: The trusted parser/scorer copy lives in a temporary directory only while
288: scoring. The archive worker grades into the store of the configured artifact
289: root that the launcher admitted. It refuses, before any selection, ledger or
290: native work, an attempt directory that is not directly below that root or whose
291: parent is a symlink.
292: Agent-written and execution bytes stay canonical and are scanned: the candidate
293: patch, native transcripts and logs, `test.log`, `grade.json` and the result
294: records.
295: 
296: For each relocated tree, the canonical root holds
297: `$artifacts/<store path>.relocation.json` (`task-input-relocation/1`). It
298: records the tree kind (`agent-view`, `grader-view` or `verifier-workspace`),
299: its store path, task ID, archive commit, archive manifest SHA-256, the archive
300: binding digest, source tree, and every file's path, Git mode, size and
301: SHA-256. A workspace manifest also names the composed effective tree and the
302: canonical `candidate.patch` path and SHA-256. The grade receipt also lists its
303: three manifests in `task_inputs`, and a scored attempt's copy of that receipt is
304: bound into the scheduler ledger through its result.
305: 
306: The audit, and the seal inventory under the same rules, verify the store after
307: the unchanged canonical scan passes:
308: 
309: - every manifest is well formed, sits at its tree's mirrored path, and is bound
310:   to a frozen `corpus.tasks[].archive_binding` with a configured
311:   `archive_roots` checkout;
312: - each store tree matches its manifest exactly; a missing, extra or changed
313:   file fails;
314: - each tree is reproduced from the pinned archive in a temporary directory:
315:   fresh agent and grader exports, and for a workspace a fresh materialization
316:   composed with the canonical candidate patch. A tree whose inventory or
317:   effective tree differs from the reproduction is not traceable and fails;
318: - every file in the store belongs to exactly one manifest;
319: - every manifest is named by exactly one export record. A name the record does
320:   not list as removed must have its verified manifest and tree, so deleting a
321:   manifest together with its tree fails, including after a failed grading. A
322:   removed name must have neither;
323: - every manifest named by a grade receipt exists with that receipt's effective
324:   tree.
325: 
326: A passing receipt then carries `task_input_relocation` (store path and one
327: summary per tree) and `checks.task_input_relocation=passed`; a seal carries the
328: same `task_input_relocation` field. An artifact root with no store, export
329: record, manifest or manifest-naming grade receipt is the historical in-root
330: layout. Its audit and
331: seal receipts keep their original shape, and any in-root copy of pinned bytes
332: is still scanned and rejected exactly as before.
333: 
334: Before approving an execution configuration for a new release, exercise the
335: procedure provider-free against every release task. These discovery commands
336: read the release and checkout from the admitted configuration; the output is a
337: fresh directory outside both the canonical root and its store:
338: 
339: ```sh
340: archive_tag="$($checkout/.venv/bin/python -B -c \
341:   'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["archive_release"]["tag"])' "$configuration")"
342: archive_release_id="$($checkout/.venv/bin/python -B -c \
343:   'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["archive_release"]["release_id"])' "$configuration")"
344: archive_root="$($checkout/.venv/bin/python -B -c \
345:   'import json,sys; print(sorted(set(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["archive_roots"].values()))[0])' "$configuration")"
346: exercise="$base/state/stage-a/retention-exercise-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
347: "$checkout/.venv/bin/python" -B "$checkout/scripts/exercise_stage_a_retention.py" \
348:   --archive "$archive_root" --release-tag "$archive_tag" --release-id "$archive_release_id" \
349:   --output "$exercise"
350: ```
351: 
352: Expected: JSON with `status=passed` and the names of tasks whose relocated
353: trees contain scanner-matching bytes. For each task the exercise runs both
354: production export sites into the store: the launcher's block-view export under
355: `<task-id>/archive-inputs/` and the grader's export and composition, with an
356: empty candidate, under `<task-id>/grade/`. It admits each binding with a
357: preserved owned image, as production does; `--fixture-only` exists only for
358: synthetic fixtures. `$exercise/retention-receipt.json` records the canonical
359: inventory and passing scan and, for each task, its relocated inventories and,
360: per file, the number of distinct scanner-matched strings and of pattern hits.
361: The matched strings themselves are not recorded. Its `execution` block states
362: zero provider requests and comparative attempts by construction (no model or
363: provider client is invoked); they are not measured. No test command runs. The
364: exercise needs a release checkout whose manifest lists every eligible task; the
365: runner itself still admits only the configured scope.
366: 
367: ### Retention failure recovery
368: 
369: A relocation failure is an audit failure: stop, preserve the canonical root,
370: the store, the ledger and the unit journal, and obtain an explicit owner
371: disposition. Never edit, move, delete or regenerate store files or manifests
372: by hand, and never move a tree into or out of `$artifacts` to make an audit
373: pass. Locate the named mismatch with:
374: 
375: ```sh
376: find "$artifacts" -name 'task-input-export.json' -exec grep -l '"failure": "' {} +
377: find "$artifacts" -name '*.relocation.json' | sort
378: find "${artifacts}.task-inputs" -type f | sort | head -n 50
379: ```
380: 
381: Compare it against a fresh provider-free exercise of the same release (above).
382: A failed export that raised has already removed its unrecorded trees and
383: still verifies; its record names the failure. An export record naming a
384: manifest that never appeared, with no `failure`, means the process stopped
385: mid-export (for example it was killed). Treat it like any interrupted attempt:
386: no automatic cleanup or replay. A changed, extra or untraceable store file
387: means the store no longer proves its bytes against the archive and is
388: diagnosed as evidence tampering or a defect.
389: Because every relocated tree is reproducible from the pinned archive and the
390: canonical candidate patches, a lost tree can be rebuilt only under a separate,
391: owner-approved and reviewed reconstruction procedure; this runbook does not
392: authorize one.
393: 
394: The #220 manual relocation was a one-time reconciliation, not this procedure; see the
395: [post-Glaze handoff](../historical/issue-notes/24/post-glaze-handoff-2026-09-29.md).
396: 
397: ## Future full-cohort launch and seal
398: 
399: The one-task #220 freeze has no block two and cannot produce a full Stage A
400: seal. For #24, first verify #219's immutable release, all 25 archival
401: inventories, owned environments, validator dispositions, and the approved
402: 23-task reviewed subset. Then produce a new exact Stage A freeze, target
403: admission, capacity plan and operator runbook. Owner approval of that freeze is
404: the single launch decision.
405: 
406: The 23-task cohort does not use this runbook's first-block stop, continuation
407: decision or `first_block_task_id`:
408: 
409: - It runs every block in order from one ledger under the per-block supervisor
410:   watchdog, advancing automatically after each clean block.
411: - A non-clean block stops the cohort fail-closed.
412: - An authenticated Claude enrollment renewal is a recorded operator recovery,
413:   modeled on the pre-launch recovery above.
414: - An offline audit covers all 161 slots before the seal.
415: 
416: The first-block audit and decision helpers bind one freeze and ledger; they
417: cannot transfer #220's audit or owner decision to this new identity. The
418: [continuous-cohort runbook](stage-a-continuous-cohort.md) covers the portable
419: preparation (configuration build, rebind, image qualification, assembly, owner
420: approval and freeze publication), dispatch, renewal, stop and resume, audit and
421: seal for the `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` scope. Run the provider-free retention exercise above
422: against every eligible release task before approving that configuration.
423: 
424: ## Focused review checks
425: 
426: These tests are credential-free and do not start a comparative trial:
427: 
428: ```sh
429: cd /home/anodyine/.local/share/agent-harness-evals/staged-execution/checkout
430: .venv/bin/python -B -m pytest -q \
431:   tests/test_stage_a_first_block.py tests/test_stage_a_launcher.py \
432:   tests/test_stage_a_execution.py tests/test_stage_scheduler.py \
433:   tests/test_task_outcomes_v2.py tests/test_task_archive.py \
434:   tests/test_task_input_retention.py
435: ```
436: 
437: Expected: all tests pass. Do not run `make check` for this individual issue; the
438: repository reserves the complete gate for the final integrated epic commit.

197:   --property="CPUQuota=${cpu}%" --property="MemoryMax=$memory" \
198:   --property="TasksMax=$tasks" --property="RuntimeMaxSec=$runtime_seconds" \
199:   --property=Nice=10 --working-directory="$checkout" \
200:   /usr/bin/env -i "PATH=$runtime_path" LANG=C.UTF-8 \
201:   "XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u)" \
202:   "$checkout/.venv/bin/python" -B "$checkout/scripts/audit_stage_a_first_block.py" audit \
203:   --freeze "$freeze" --configuration "$configuration" --ledger "$ledger" \
204:   --admission-directory "$admission" --approval "$approval" \
205:   --host-profile "$profile" --trusted-host-digest "$trusted_host_digest" \
206:   --artifacts "$artifacts"
207: 
208: systemctl --user show "$unit" -p MainPID -p SubState -p Result -p ExecMainStatus
209: journalctl --user -u "$unit" --no-pager
210: ```
211: 
212: Expected: the audit exits successfully and immutably writes
213: `$artifacts/first-block-audit.json`. The receipt binds the clean execution commit,
214: host/profile, final freeze, seven-arm index, target admission and owner approval,
215: runtime inventory, resource limits, canonical paths, complete scheduler
216: checkpoint, account reservation history, one task-outcome-v2 record for every attempted slot,
217: exact typed unstarted dispositions, every retained artifact hash, secret scan,
218: hidden-score isolation, and quiescent reservations, images, containers, and
219: volumes. An archive-bound root also passes the task-input retention check
220: described below. Running the same audit again against the unchanged checkpoint
221: reproduces the identical receipt. Any changed input or history is rejected.
222: 
223: Scheduler `started_at` records the reservation before admission checks. Launch
224: intent `started_at` records the later write immediately before native execution.
225: The auditor compares timezone-aware instants and requires reservation time ≤
226: intent time ≤ scheduler completion time. These are distinct events; their text
227: and instants need not be equal. Both original timestamps remain in the retained
228: evidence. An intent outside the reserved interval, or a missing, malformed or
229: timezone-free timestamp, is rejected.
230: 
231: An owner may explicitly resume a held Claude reservation rejected because its
232: account-policy receipt expired **before native execution started**. This narrow
233: recovery keeps the original intent and interruption untouched, with no native
234: artifacts, no additional reservation, and no refund. A new sibling directory
235: `<lease-id>-prelaunch-resume-r1` holds the first native execution. The canonical
236: artifact root retains `prelaunch-recovery-<lease-id>.json`, binding both directory
237: identities, the original inventory, interruption, freeze, configuration and clean
238: execution revision. It also retains the explicit restart decision and new owner
239: account-policy confirmation; the renewed enrollment must keep the same account,
240: token, tier and credit/isolation settings. The original receipt is not extended
241: or overwritten. The audit checks the chronology and both intents against the
242: single reservation, and includes the complete recovery record in the disposition.
243: Any prior native evidence, changed history, missing confirmation or unbound
244: recovery record rejects this path. This is an explicit operator recovery, not an
245: automatic replay feature; it does not authorize later blocks.
246: 
247: Stop after audit even when it passes:
248: 
249: ```sh
250: systemctl --user stop "$unit"
251: ```
252: 
253: No audit failure authorizes continuation. Preserve the failed unit and evidence,
254: diagnose the specific mismatch, and obtain an explicit owner disposition. Deleting
255: the ledger, moving to another artifact directory, or initializing a replacement
256: cohort cannot pass because the admitted profile and freeze bind the original
257: canonical paths and identities.
258: 
259: ## Task-input retention
260: 
261: The audit and seal hash and secret-scan every regular file under the canonical
262: artifact root `$artifacts` with the unchanged `security.SECRET_PATTERNS`. Pinned
263: task sources can legitimately contain credential-shaped examples, so
264: archive-bound execution never writes task-source-derived trees there. The
265: launcher and grader create them directly in the sibling task-input store
266: `${artifacts}.task-inputs`, at the same relative path they would otherwise have
267: had under `$artifacts`. Nothing is moved after the fact, and the scanner is
268: neither weakened nor allow-listed.
269: 
270: | Tree | Created by | Store path |
271: | --- | --- | --- |
272: | Block agent and grader views | launcher, once per block | `archive-inputs-<uuid>/{agent,grader}` |
273: | Grading agent and grader views | grader, once per attempt | `<lease-id>/verification/grade/{agent,grader}` |
274: | Composed verifier workspace | grader, once per attempt | `<lease-id>/verification/grade/verifier-workspace` |
275: 
276: Before creating any tree, each export writes a canonical export record,
277: `task-input-export.json` (`task-input-export/1`), in its canonical directory
278: (`archive-inputs-<uuid>/` or `<lease-id>/verification/grade/`). It names every
279: relocation manifest the export will produce. If the export raises, every
280: planned tree that has no manifest yet is removed from the store, and the record
281: is rewritten to list those names under `removed` with the error type under
282: `failure`. Trees recorded before the failure, for example the views of an
283: attempt whose owned-image grading later fails, are retained and verified.
284: 
285: The retained verifier workspace is exactly the composed effective tree. Its Git
286: metadata is grading scaffolding and is removed before the tree is recorded.
287: The trusted parser/scorer copy lives in a temporary directory only while
288: scoring. The archive worker grades into the store of the configured artifact
289: root that the launcher admitted. It refuses, before any selection, ledger or
290: native work, an attempt directory that is not directly below that root or whose
291: parent is a symlink.
292: Agent-written and execution bytes stay canonical and are scanned: the candidate
293: patch, native transcripts and logs, `test.log`, `grade.json` and the result
294: records.
295: 
296: For each relocated tree, the canonical root holds
297: `$artifacts/<store path>.relocation.json` (`task-input-relocation/1`). It
298: records the tree kind (`agent-view`, `grader-view` or `verifier-workspace`),
299: its store path, task ID, archive commit, archive manifest SHA-256, the archive
300: binding digest, source tree, and every file's path, Git mode, size and
301: SHA-256. A workspace manifest also names the composed effective tree and the
302: canonical `candidate.patch` path and SHA-256. The grade receipt also lists its
303: three manifests in `task_inputs`, and a scored attempt's copy of that receipt is
304: bound into the scheduler ledger through its result.
305: 
306: The audit, and the seal inventory under the same rules, verify the store after
307: the unchanged canonical scan passes:
308: 
309: - every manifest is well formed, sits at its tree's mirrored path, and is bound
310:   to a frozen `corpus.tasks[].archive_binding` with a configured
311:   `archive_roots` checkout;
312: - each store tree matches its manifest exactly; a missing, extra or changed
313:   file fails;
314: - each tree is reproduced from the pinned archive in a temporary directory:
315:   fresh agent and grader exports, and for a workspace a fresh materialization
316:   composed with the canonical candidate patch. A tree whose inventory or
317:   effective tree differs from the reproduction is not traceable and fails;
318: - every file in the store belongs to exactly one manifest;
319: - every manifest is named by exactly one export record. A name the record does
320:   not list as removed must have its verified manifest and tree, so deleting a
321:   manifest together with its tree fails, including after a failed grading. A
322:   removed name must have neither;
323: - every manifest named by a grade receipt exists with that receipt's effective
324:   tree.
325: 
326: A passing receipt then carries `task_input_relocation` (store path and one
327: summary per tree) and `checks.task_input_relocation=passed`; a seal carries the
328: same `task_input_relocation` field. An artifact root with no store, export
329: record, manifest or manifest-naming grade receipt is the historical in-root
330: layout. Its audit and
331: seal receipts keep their original shape, and any in-root copy of pinned bytes
332: is still scanned and rejected exactly as before.
333: 
334: Before approving an execution configuration for a new release, exercise the
335: procedure provider-free against every release task. These discovery commands
336: read the release and checkout from the admitted configuration; the output is a
337: fresh directory outside both the canonical root and its store:
338: 
339: ```sh
340: archive_tag="$($checkout/.venv/bin/python -B -c \
341:   'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["archive_release"]["tag"])' "$configuration")"
342: archive_release_id="$($checkout/.venv/bin/python -B -c \
343:   'import json,sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["archive_release"]["release_id"])' "$configuration")"
344: archive_root="$($checkout/.venv/bin/python -B -c \
345:   'import json,sys; print(sorted(set(json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))["archive_roots"].values()))[0])' "$configuration")"
346: exercise="$base/state/stage-a/retention-exercise-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
347: "$checkout/.venv/bin/python" -B "$checkout/scripts/exercise_stage_a_retention.py" \
348:   --archive "$archive_root" --release-tag "$archive_tag" --release-id "$archive_release_id" \
349:   --output "$exercise"
350: ```
351: 
352: Expected: JSON with `status=passed` and the names of tasks whose relocated
353: trees contain scanner-matching bytes. For each task the exercise runs both
354: production export sites into the store: the launcher's block-view export under
355: `<task-id>/archive-inputs/` and the grader's export and composition, with an
356: empty candidate, under `<task-id>/grade/`. It admits each binding with a
357: preserved owned image, as production does; `--fixture-only` exists only for
358: synthetic fixtures. `$exercise/retention-receipt.json` records the canonical
359: inventory and passing scan and, for each task, its relocated inventories and,
360: per file, the number of distinct scanner-matched strings and of pattern hits.
361: The matched strings themselves are not recorded. Its `execution` block states
362: zero provider requests and comparative attempts by construction (no model or
363: provider client is invoked); they are not measured. No test command runs. The
364: exercise needs a release checkout whose manifest lists every eligible task; the
365: runner itself still admits only the configured scope.
366: 
367: ### Retention failure recovery
368: 
369: A relocation failure is an audit failure: stop, preserve the canonical root,
370: the store, the ledger and the unit journal, and obtain an explicit owner
371: disposition. Never edit, move, delete or regenerate store files or manifests
372: by hand, and never move a tree into or out of `$artifacts` to make an audit
373: pass. Locate the named mismatch with:
374: 
375: ```sh
376: find "$artifacts" -name 'task-input-export.json' -exec grep -l '"failure": "' {} +
377: find "$artifacts" -name '*.relocation.json' | sort
378: find "${artifacts}.task-inputs" -type f | sort | head -n 50
379: ```
380: 
381: Compare it against a fresh provider-free exercise of the same release (above).
382: A failed export that raised has already removed its unrecorded trees and
383: still verifies; its record names the failure. An export record naming a
384: manifest that never appeared, with no `failure`, means the process stopped
385: mid-export (for example it was killed). Treat it like any interrupted attempt:
386: no automatic cleanup or replay. A changed, extra or untraceable store file
387: means the store no longer proves its bytes against the archive and is
388: diagnosed as evidence tampering or a defect.
389: Because every relocated tree is reproducible from the pinned archive and the
390: canonical candidate patches, a lost tree can be rebuilt only under a separate,
391: owner-approved and reviewed reconstruction procedure; this runbook does not
392: authorize one.
393: 
394: The #220 manual relocation was a one-time reconciliation, not this procedure; see the
395: [post-Glaze handoff](../historical/issue-notes/24/post-glaze-handoff-2026-09-29.md).
396: 
397: ## Future full-cohort launch and seal
398: 
399: The one-task #220 freeze has no block two and cannot produce a full Stage A
400: seal. For #24, first verify #219's immutable release, all 25 archival
401: inventories, owned environments, validator dispositions, and the approved
402: 23-task reviewed subset. Then produce a new exact Stage A freeze, target
403: admission, capacity plan and operator runbook. Owner approval of that freeze is
404: the single launch decision.
405: 
406: The 23-task cohort does not use this runbook's first-block stop, continuation
407: decision or `first_block_task_id`:
408: 
409: - It runs every block in order from one ledger under the per-block supervisor
410:   watchdog, advancing automatically after each clean block.
411: - A non-clean block stops the cohort fail-closed.
412: - An authenticated Claude enrollment renewal is a recorded operator recovery,
413:   modeled on the pre-launch recovery above.
414: - An offline audit covers all 161 slots before the seal.
415: 
416: The first-block audit and decision helpers bind one freeze and ledger; they
417: cannot transfer #220's audit or owner decision to this new identity. The
418: [continuous-cohort runbook](stage-a-continuous-cohort.md) covers the portable
419: preparation (configuration build, rebind, image qualification, assembly, owner
420: approval and freeze publication), dispatch, renewal, stop and resume, audit and
421: seal for the `archive-stage-a-cohort/1` scope. Run the provider-free retention exercise above
422: against every eligible release task before approving that configuration.
423: 
424: ## Focused review checks
425: 
426: These tests are credential-free and do not start a comparative trial:
427: 
428: ```sh
429: cd /home/anodyine/.local/share/agent-harness-evals/staged-execution/checkout
430: .venv/bin/python -B -m pytest -q \

433:   tests/test_task_outcomes_v2.py tests/test_task_archive.py \
434:   tests/test_task_input_retention.py
435: ```
436: 
437: Expected: all tests pass. Do not run `make check` for this individual issue; the
438: repository reserves the complete gate for the final integrated epic commit.

101: 
102: ### Status

105: That outcome is not retried. The owner decided on 2026-10-08 to keep one
106: attempt per slot, as ADR 0016 and the v5 contract freeze it, and #288
107: (retries) was declined. The reasons:
108:
