110:   `capability_unknown`, which sits on the arm's side of the futility rule.
111: - **It should be rare.** It was then read as a hang on the final poll. The
112:   corrected mechanism below is a replaced server, whose trigger is unconfirmed.
113: - **The cost is high.** Retrying would change the launcher, the Claude
114:   baseline, research allowance sizing, and audit and seal.
115: 
116: #293, which would have recovered a finished process's output, was closed: the
117: process had not finished. #296 makes every native sandbox failure a recorded
118: outcome, stops the orphaned agent before capture, and keeps the server's state
119: so that the next failure can name its trigger.
120: 
121: The Mechanism section below records retained evidence of a second way to lose
122: a process: the sandbox-tools server being replaced while the agent still runs.
123: Recovering a lost final poll does not cover that case.
124: 
125: ### The stop
126: 
127: The facts in this section were observed on asrock by the owner, as reported
128: in #283. The pids and the kill's timing come from the retained
129: `native/inspect.json`.
130: 
131: - **When and where.** At 2026-10-08T10:56:49Z, in block 5's first slot:
132:   actual order 29, `codex-muse-spark-1.3-contributor` ×
133:   `moonD4rk__HackBrowserData-571`, lease
134:   `65c0ccf6-817e-5042-a0d0-6851a2ff7928`. Blocks 1–4 had advanced normally.
135: - **What failed.**
136:   - The launcher started Codex through Inspect's `exec_remote` at
137:     10:53:50.68Z. The sandbox-tools server (pid 414) returned job pid 428.
138:   - A poll then failed with `RuntimeError('No job found with pid 428')`. The
139:     failing poll is not timed (see the retry-log check).
140:   - The adapter's kill, sent at 10:56:47.29Z (ack_seq 43), got the same answer
141:     as a JSON-RPC error by 10:56:47.62Z. The sample recorded the error at
142:     10:56:47.89Z.
143: - **How the cohort stopped.** The exception escaped the Codex adapter as an
144:   Inspect sample error. `_run_native` then raised `native task did not
145:   complete`, `run_block` wrote `interrupted.json`, and the unit failed with an
146:   unreconciled active attempt. The cohort cannot resume.
147: - **Host state.** Sandbox cleanup was confirmed: no containers or networks
148:   remained on the eval Docker daemon. There was no OOM on the host.
149: 
150: ### Mechanism
151: 
152: Read from the pinned source (inspect-ai 0.3.261, sandbox tools 1.2.1):
153: 
154: - **Each poll is one exec.** It is a `sandbox.exec` with a 120 s timeout and
155:   `timeout_retry=True`. On a timeout, the Docker sandbox silently re-runs the
156:   exec, up to twice.
157: - **The server forgets finished jobs.** `Controller.poll` retires a job as soon
158:   as it reports `completed` or `killed`, and `_get_job` never consults retired
159:   jobs.
160: - **So a re-run final poll fails.** If the hung exec had already delivered the
161:   final poll, its re-run answers `No job found`. The poll's own retry,
162:   `stop_after_delay(30)` measured from the first attempt, re-raises at once.
163: 
164: The timeline is consistent with that sequence. A poll at about 10:54:47Z hung
165: for 120 s, and its re-run found the job retired. The hang itself is inferred
166: from the timeline, not observed. #283 was fixed on that account.
167: 
168: **The retained evidence contradicts it.**
169: - **Codex had not finished.** The provider-proxy capture
170:   (`native/wsrf3ww0.capture/transport.jsonl`) shows 38 Codex requests from
171:   10:53:51Z, 1–14 seconds apart, through the supposed hang. The last one is at
172:   10:56:47.428Z, after the kill was sent.
173: - **So the job could not have been retired as finished.** A job is retired
174:   only after its process exits, and pid 428 was Codex itself: `/bin/sh -c`,
175:   `env` and `sh -c 'exec "$@"'` all `exec`.
176: 
177: **The server was most likely replaced while Codex ran.** Read from the same
178: pinned source:
179: - **The client restarts a server it can't reach.** Before every call, the
180:   sandbox-tools client checks the server's socket in `/tmp/sandbox-tools/`. If
181:   it cannot reach it, it starts a new server with an empty job registry.
182: - **The old job runs on.** Jobs are plain children of the old server, so they
183:   keep running as orphans.
184: - **This fits the stop.** The kill was answered by a live server, with a
185:   JSON-RPC error rather than a transport failure. Codex kept calling the
186:   provider until the container was removed.
187: 
188: **The trigger is unconfirmed.** The adapter kept none of Codex's stream. The
189: candidates are all within the agent's reach:
190: - **Killing the server.** The agent runs as the same user as the server, in one
191:   process namespace, with Codex's own sandbox bypassed.
192: - **Removing its state.** The server's socket and pid file are on the agent's
193:   64 MiB `/tmp` tmpfs.
194: - **A server crash.** The host showed no OOM.
195: 
196: **Settling it next time.** From #296 on, a lost process records, before
197: teardown, the server identified when the job started and whether it is still
198: alive, the current server, the state directory's listing and the tail of
199: `server-stderr.log`. A different current server confirms a replacement, and
200: the partial stream that #283 persists shows the agent's last commands.
201: 
202: ### Prevention: agents run unprivileged
203: 
204: The owner decided on 2026-10-08 (#296) that every arm's agent will run as an
205: unprivileged user, with the sandbox-tools server out of its reach. Running all
206: arms at the same privilege level also keeps the comparison even. Today every
207: arm's agent runs as the container's root user, like the server; only Claude
208: Code's MCP bridge drops to another user. The change is tracked separately
209: (#300); until it lands, a failure is recorded and the agent stopped, but
210: not prevented.
211: 
212: ### Retry-log check
213: 
214: The owner inspected the interrupted sample's `native/inspect.json` once asrock
215: was reachable again. It holds no `logger` events, only 44 `sandbox` events,
216: spans, `sample_init` and the error. Polls run under `no_events()`, so the
217: transcript can neither confirm nor rule out a `Retrying docker compose command
218: after TimeoutError` re-run.
219: 
220: From #283 on, the sandbox transport never re-runs a poll. The native stream
221: re-polls a timed-out poll itself, and the adapter records the count as
222: `diagnostics.native_process.poll_timeouts`. A future stop therefore names its
223: poll timeouts directly.
224: 
225: ### Upstream
226: 
227: Inspect 0.3.277 (2026-10-06) adds opt-in `poll_timeout_recovery`, which
228: re-polls after a timeout. Its sandbox tools v33 also make kill safer after a
229: process has exited. Neither keeps a retired job answerable: a lost final poll
230: still raises, as "the process most likely ended during the stall". A pin bump
231: would therefore not have prevented this stop.
232: 
233: ## Checkout fetch timeout between slots (#281)
234: 
235: Fixed by #281: dispatch revalidates the host without fetching origin.
236: 
237: At 2026-10-08T00:01:09-04:00, between orders 5 and 6, the supervisor exited
238: 1 while re-validating the host profile. The checkout-identity check's
239: `git fetch --no-tags origin refs/heads/main` timed out after 60 seconds:
240: 
241: ```text
242: subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['git', 'fetch', '--no-tags', 'origin', 'refs/heads/main']' timed out after 60 seconds
243: ```
244: 
245: The unit started again at 00:06:15. Its restart counter read 1 only at the
246: next block boundary, so that start was not a systemd restart. Order 6 began at
247: 00:07:26, and no slot was lost.

82: Replayed through the fixed boundary, order 24's retained grade keeps all
83: 26,864 statuses. The two names persist as `.../[REDACTED]` and
84: `.../[REDACTED]#2`, and nothing secret-shaped remains.
85: 
86: ## Why image qualification missed both (#282)
87: 
88: Image qualification checked image fit, the native executables, the sanitizer
89: and the Claude adapter's workspace steps. It graded nothing and never built a
90: task:
91: 
92: - **httrack.** No workspace was captured in the state an agent's build leaves
93:   it.
94: - **gh-aw.** The archive's reference-patch controls are graded in the task
95:   archive repository, whose raw control logs are not retained. They never pass
96:   through this repository's persistence redaction.
97: 
98: Qualification now does both (ADRs 0021 and 0022).
99: 
100: ## Stop: a lost `exec_remote` job (#283)
101: 
102: ### Status
103: 
104: Fixed by #283: a lost native process is now a recorded outcome, not a stop.
105: That outcome is not retried. The owner decided on 2026-10-08 to keep one
106: attempt per slot, as ADR 0016 and the v5 contract freeze it, and #288
107: (retries) was declined. The reasons:
108: 
109: - **A lost slot can't wrongly cut an arm.** It counts as
110:   `capability_unknown`, which sits on the arm's side of the futility rule.
111: - **It should be rare.** It was then read as a hang on the final poll. The
112:   corrected mechanism below is a replaced server, whose trigger is unconfirmed.
113: - **The cost is high.** Retrying would change the launcher, the Claude
114:   baseline, research allowance sizing, and audit and seal.
115: 
116: #293, which would have recovered a finished process's output, was closed: the
117: process had not finished. #296 makes every native sandbox failure a recorded
118: outcome, stops the orphaned agent before capture, and keeps the server's state
119: so that the next failure can name its trigger.
120: 
121: The Mechanism section below records retained evidence of a second way to lose
122: a process: the sandbox-tools server being replaced while the agent still runs.
123: Recovering a lost final poll does not cover that case.
124: 
125: ### The stop
126: 
127: The facts in this section were observed on asrock by the owner, as reported
128: in #283. The pids and the kill's timing come from the retained
129: `native/inspect.json`.
130: 
131: - **When and where.** At 2026-10-08T10:56:49Z, in block 5's first slot:
132:   actual order 29, `codex-muse-spark-1.3-contributor` ×
133:   `moonD4rk__HackBrowserData-571`, lease
134:   `65c0ccf6-817e-5042-a0d0-6851a2ff7928`. Blocks 1–4 had advanced normally.
135: - **What failed.**
136:   - The launcher started Codex through Inspect's `exec_remote` at
137:     10:53:50.68Z. The sandbox-tools server (pid 414) returned job pid 428.
138:   - A poll then failed with `RuntimeError('No job found with pid 428')`. The
139:     failing poll is not timed (see the retry-log check).
140:   - The adapter's kill, sent at 10:56:47.29Z (ack_seq 43), got the same answer
141:     as a JSON-RPC error by 10:56:47.62Z. The sample recorded the error at
142:     10:56:47.89Z.
143: - **How the cohort stopped.** The exception escaped the Codex adapter as an
144:   Inspect sample error. `_run_native` then raised `native task did not
145:   complete`, `run_block` wrote `interrupted.json`, and the unit failed with an
146:   unreconciled active attempt. The cohort cannot resume.
147: - **Host state.** Sandbox cleanup was confirmed: no containers or networks
148:   remained on the eval Docker daemon. There was no OOM on the host.
149: 
150: ### Mechanism
151: 
152: Read from the pinned source (inspect-ai 0.3.261, sandbox tools 1.2.1):
153: 
154: - **Each poll is one exec.** It is a `sandbox.exec` with a 120 s timeout and
155:   `timeout_retry=True`. On a timeout, the Docker sandbox silently re-runs the
156:   exec, up to twice.
157: - **The server forgets finished jobs.** `Controller.poll` retires a job as soon
158:   as it reports `completed` or `killed`, and `_get_job` never consults retired
159:   jobs.
160: - **So a re-run final poll fails.** If the hung exec had already delivered the
161:   final poll, its re-run answers `No job found`. The poll's own retry,
162:   `stop_after_delay(30)` measured from the first attempt, re-raises at once.
163: 
164: The timeline is consistent with that sequence. A poll at about 10:54:47Z hung
165: for 120 s, and its re-run found the job retired. The hang itself is inferred
166: from the timeline, not observed. #283 was fixed on that account.
167: 
168: **The retained evidence contradicts it.**
169: - **Codex had not finished.** The provider-proxy capture
170:   (`native/wsrf3ww0.capture/transport.jsonl`) shows 38 Codex requests from
171:   10:53:51Z, 1–14 seconds apart, through the supposed hang. The last one is at
172:   10:56:47.428Z, after the kill was sent.
173: - **So the job could not have been retired as finished.** A job is retired
174:   only after its process exits, and pid 428 was Codex itself: `/bin/sh -c`,
175:   `env` and `sh -c 'exec "$@"'` all `exec`.
176: 
177: **The server was most likely replaced while Codex ran.** Read from the same
178: pinned source:
179: - **The client restarts a server it can't reach.** Before every call, the
180:   sandbox-tools client checks the server's socket in `/tmp/sandbox-tools/`. If
181:   it cannot reach it, it starts a new server with an empty job registry.
182: - **The old job runs on.** Jobs are plain children of the old server, so they
183:   keep running as orphans.
184: - **This fits the stop.** The kill was answered by a live server, with a
185:   JSON-RPC error rather than a transport failure. Codex kept calling the
186:   provider until the container was removed.
187: 
188: **The trigger is unconfirmed.** The adapter kept none of Codex's stream. The
189: candidates are all within the agent's reach:
190: - **Killing the server.** The agent runs as the same user as the server, in one
191:   process namespace, with Codex's own sandbox bypassed.
192: - **Removing its state.** The server's socket and pid file are on the agent's
193:   64 MiB `/tmp` tmpfs.
194: - **A server crash.** The host showed no OOM.
195: 
196: **Settling it next time.** From #296 on, a lost process records, before
197: teardown, the server identified when the job started and whether it is still
198: alive, the current server, the state directory's listing and the tail of
199: `server-stderr.log`. A different current server confirms a replacement, and
200: the partial stream that #283 persists shows the agent's last commands.
201: 
202: ### Prevention: agents run unprivileged
203: 
204: The owner decided on 2026-10-08 (#296) that every arm's agent will run as an
205: unprivileged user, with the sandbox-tools server out of its reach. Running all
206: arms at the same privilege level also keeps the comparison even. Today every
207: arm's agent runs as the container's root user, like the server; only Claude
208: Code's MCP bridge drops to another user. The change is tracked separately
209: (#300); until it lands, a failure is recorded and the agent stopped, but
210: not prevented.
211: 
212: ### Retry-log check
213: 
214: The owner inspected the interrupted sample's `native/inspect.json` once asrock
215: was reachable again. It holds no `logger` events, only 44 `sandbox` events,
216: spans, `sample_init` and the error. Polls run under `no_events()`, so the
217: transcript can neither confirm nor rule out a `Retrying docker compose command
218: after TimeoutError` re-run.
219: 
220: From #283 on, the sandbox transport never re-runs a poll. The native stream
221: re-polls a timed-out poll itself, and the adapter records the count as
222: `diagnostics.native_process.poll_timeouts`. A future stop therefore names its
223: poll timeouts directly.
224: 
225: ### Upstream
226: 
227: Inspect 0.3.277 (2026-10-06) adds opt-in `poll_timeout_recovery`, which
228: re-polls after a timeout. Its sandbox tools v33 also make kill safer after a
229: process has exited. Neither keeps a retired job answerable: a lost final poll
230: still raises, as "the process most likely ended during the stall". A pin bump
231: would therefore not have prevented this stop.
232: 
233: ## Checkout fetch timeout between slots (#281)
234: 
235: Fixed by #281: dispatch revalidates the host without fetching origin.
236: 
237: At 2026-10-08T00:01:09-04:00, between orders 5 and 6, the supervisor exited
238: 1 while re-validating the host profile. The checkout-identity check's
239: `git fetch --no-tags origin refs/heads/main` timed out after 60 seconds:
240: 
241: ```text
242: subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['git', 'fetch', '--no-tags', 'origin', 'refs/heads/main']' timed out after 60 seconds
243: ```
244: 
245: The unit started again at 00:06:15. Its restart counter read 1 only at the
246: next block boundary, so that start was not a systemd restart. Order 6 began at
247: 00:07:26, and no slot was lost.

10: # Screen Stage A on the 23 reviewed archive tasks
11: 
12: Stage A screens the seven standard arms on the 23 tasks in the reviewed subset
13: of the full `multilang-task-archive` release, with one repetition and one
14: attempt per slot: 161 scheduled slots. Independent review left two of the 25
15: selected tasks `unresolved`, and both are dropped without replacement:
16: 
17: | Task | Language | Review decision |
18: | --- | --- | --- |
19: | `AOMediaCodec__libavif-3300` | C | Archive issue #15, PR #55, 2026-09-29: `original-v1` scores a partial `tonemap`/`combine` candidate 1; the proposed `metadata-flags-v1` correction was not adopted. |
20: | `yvgude__lean-ctx-1180` | Rust | Archive issue #20, PR #60, 2026-10-02: `original-v1` accepts an incomplete Context Contents UI candidate and rejects a credible alternative for omitting a reference-authored test name. |
21: 
22: The corpus is bound to the reviewed archive release: its tag, release ID,
23: manifest SHA-256 and archive commit, plus each task's complete archive binding.
24: No dataset corpus file is created for it. The release is pinned at or after
25: archive commit `1c5a58f8b0227b5cfa1be85542493af90c6caab7`, whose grader view
26: carries the selected test patch as `validation/tests.patch`. #219 verifies the
27: release's harness adoption one task at a time: for each of the 23 bindings,
28: `task_archive.inspect` and production `admit` must pass. Consuming the release
29: as one multi-task release is a separate harness capability.
30: 
31: The 23 retained tasks keep their v3 task IDs, source revisions, task text and
32: repositories. Each is graded by the validator its archive review selected. The
33: executable allocation is `c=2`, `cpp=4`, `go=4`, `js=3`, `rust=2`, `java=0`,
34: `ts=4`, `cs=4` across 23 distinct repositories. The oldest retained
35: `created_at` is `2026-04-03T09:27:24Z` (`gfx-rs__wgpu-9367`), unchanged from
36: v3. Reports disclose the reduced C and Rust strata alongside the absence of
37: Java.
38: 
39: Slot counts derive from the frozen corpus: tasks × the seven standard arms ×
40: one repetition. Validators, preflight receipts, launchers, audits, seals and
41: the `stage-a-capability-disposition/1` artifact compare against that derived
42: value, never a literal. For this corpus the disposition holds 161 records,
43: 23 per arm.
44: 
45: The futility gate is unchanged as an absolute rule. An arm is
46: capability-futile only when `resolved + capability_unknown + unstarted <= 1`
47: after all 23 of its slots reconcile; an arm whose upper bound is at least 2/23
48: survives. One task is 1/23 of an arm's denominator, about 4.35 percentage
49: points, and reports say so.
50: 
51: The cohort runs every scheduled block in order from one ledger, under one
52: admitted configuration and one owner-approved numerical freeze. Approval of
53: that freeze is the only launch decision. There is no first-block stop, no
54: `first_block_task_id`, no first-block gate and no owner go/no-go between
55: blocks.
56: 
57: Each block runs under the existing per-block supervisor watchdog
58: (`SUPERVISOR_POLICY` in `stage_a_execution.py`); no runtime is sized for the
59: whole cohort. When a block completes cleanly, the launcher starts the next
60: block from the same ledger under the same admitted supervisor policy, with no
61: operator action. A block that does not complete cleanly, including a watchdog
62: stop, stops the cohort fail-closed for diagnosis. An uncertain or active
63: attempt is never replayed. The ledger is never reset. An infrastructure stop
64: retains the ledger and evidence. Resuming the same ledger requires the same
65: admitted configuration and is a recovery, not a new approval.
66: 
67: Authenticated Claude enrollment renewal during the run is a recorded operator
68: recovery, not an owner go/no-go. It follows the pre-launch recovery in the
69: [first-block gate runbook](../../runbooks/stage-a-first-block-gate.md). A
70: renewal:
71: 
72: - keeps the same account, token, tier and credit/isolation settings;
73: - authenticates against the frozen identities;
74: - carries a new recorded account-policy confirmation;
75: - never extends or overwrites the original receipt;
76: - adds no reservation or refund;
77: - is bound into the ledger and evidence.
78: 
79: Without a valid renewal, a pending Claude turn that the current receipt cannot
80: cover fails closed before reservation. A renewal with a changed identity is
81: rejected.
82: 
83: After every slot is terminal or explicitly unstarted, an offline audit covers
84: all 161 slots, including each renewal's chronology, and #24 seals the cohort.
85: 
86: `stephenberry__glaze-2731` is one of the 23 and runs as fresh slots. The #155
87: and #220 Glaze blocks, with their first-block stops, audits and owner
88: decisions, remain separately reported historical evidence. Neither becomes a
89: prefix, a slot or a result of the new ledger.
90: 
91: The exclusion is outcome-independent. Both dispositions are task-validator
92: review findings judged against task-visible requirements with constructed
93: review candidates, and no comparative trial has run on either task. The
94: libavif review states that its candidates were written for the review, not
95: taken from a task-solving agent attempt. Glaze is the only task with
96: comparative outcomes, and it is retained. Dropping rather than replacing
97: follows the v5 replacement rule: replacement is allowed only for a validation
98: failure found before any comparative outcome, and never after the first trial
99: begins. Stage A trials began with the #155 block, and a replacement would also
100: need its own archive import and review. A proportional futility threshold
101: would round to zero or one possible resolution at this size and would change
102: the rule after outcomes from one task are known. Two audited Glaze blocks have
103: exercised the launch path, including archive-bound grading; fail-closed
104: recovery rules, not further approvals, protect the remaining blocks.
105: 
106: ## Consequences
107: 
108: - This supersedes the 25-task and 175-slot counts in
109:   [ADR-0010](0010-stage-multilang-screening-before-expansion.md) and
110:   [ADR-0012](0012-add-claude-code-to-staged-multilang.md), the C and Rust
111:   strata of [ADR-0015](0015-record-stage-a-successor-corpus-allocation.md),
112:   and the "ordinary 25-task Stage A contract" in
113:   [ADR-0014](0014-scope-archive-first-block-execution.md). ADR-0014's one-task
114:   first-block scope remains valid for its own freezes. The
115:   [v5 contract](../../contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md) carries the
116:   amended passages. The seven standard arms, one repetition, the absolute
117:   gate, the separate Stage B freeze and the no-pooling rule remain in force.
118: - The `swe-bench-live-multilang-stage-a-v3` corpus, its manifest digest
119:   `sha256:9dfb019c4f81e4ac4dd64a252e6ffe0ce08bc3be9238d37e656808f308f8072b`,
120:   and every earlier freeze, ledger, approval, audit, seal and receipt stay
121:   unchanged.
122: - The full release's adoption record names exactly the 23 eligible tasks and
123:   records the two exclusions with their review evidence.
124: - #24 prepares the Stage A freeze from that adoption record and owns Stage A
125:   seal accounting. #50 owns only the Stage B freeze.
126: - Executable enforcement is not implemented yet and is pending
127:   [#229](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/229). That covers derived slot counts, the multi-task
128:   archive scope, the continuous run with automatic advance, enrollment
129:   renewal, and the full-cohort audit and seal. Until it lands, the harness
130:   accepts only 25-task freezes on the historical dataset path and the one-task
131:   `archive-first-block/1` scope, so a 23-task freeze cannot validate.
132: - A new freeze also needs a reviewed result-root retention procedure for task
133:   source and workspace trees
134:   ([#230](https://tea.kyle-merritt.com/anodyine/agent-harness-evals/issues/230)). It is exercised provider-free against all 23
135:   release task sources, without weakening the global secret scanner.
136: - This decision grants no execution approval. Fresh admission, a reconciled
137:   research and provider capacity plan, the numerical freeze and owner approval
138:   of that freeze remain separate.
139: 
140: ## Alternatives considered
141: 
142: - Replace each dropped task with the next same-language repository. Rejected:
143:   barred after the first trial, and it would add unreviewed tasks.
144: - Keep both tasks under `original-v1`. Rejected: review showed each validator
145:   accepts an incorrect candidate, and lean-ctx's also rejects a credible one.
146: - Adopt the exploratory corrections. Rejected by the owner reviews.
147: - Scale the futility threshold to the smaller corpus. Rejected: the gate is
148:   absolute by design.
149: - Keep a first-block stop and continuation go/no-go. Rejected: the launch path
150:   is already audited, and fail-closed recovery covers later blocks.
151: - Size one supervised runtime for the whole cohort. Rejected: per-block
152:   watchdogs keep each failure bounded.
153: - Treat enrollment expiry as an owner go/no-go. Rejected: an
154:   identity-preserving renewal is an operator recovery.
155: - Write a 23-task dataset corpus file. Rejected: archive tasks never fall back
156:   to dataset rows.
157: 
158: ## Decision evidence
159: 
160: - Archive manifest at `multilang-task-archive` `a64c16b`: 25 tasks, 23 in the
161:   reviewed subset (20 `verified-corrected`, 3 `verified-unchanged`,
162:   2 `unresolved`). `manifest.json` is unchanged at `1c5a58f`.
163: - `tasks/AOMediaCodec__libavif-3300/review/assessment.md` and
164:   `tasks/yvgude__lean-ctx-1180/review/assessment.md` in that archive.
165: - [Post-Glaze #24 handoff](../../historical/issue-notes/24/post-glaze-handoff-2026-09-29.md):
166:   175 slots apply only if all 25 tasks remain eligible, and the Glaze block is
167:   never a prefix of a new ledger.

43: 23 per arm.

46: capability-futile only when `resolved + capability_unknown + unstarted <= 1`

48: survives. One task is 1/23 of an arm's denominator, about 4.35 percentage
49: points, and reports say so.

52: admitted configuration and one owner-approved numerical freeze. Approval of

60: block from the same ledger under the same admitted supervisor policy, with no
61: operator action. A block that does not complete cleanly, including a watchdog

63: attempt is never replayed. The ledger is never reset. An infrastructure stop
64: retains the ledger and evidence. Resuming the same ledger requires the same
65: admitted configuration and is a recovery, not a new approval.

68: recovery, not an owner go/no-go. It follows the pre-launch recovery in the
69: [first-block gate runbook](../../runbooks/stage-a-first-block-gate.md). A
70: renewal:

72: - keeps the same account, token, tier and credit/isolation settings;
73: - authenticates against the frozen identities;
74: - carries a new recorded account-policy confirmation;
75: - never extends or overwrites the original receipt;
76: - adds no reservation or refund;

80: cover fails closed before reservation. A renewal with a changed identity is
81: rejected.

6: 
7: # Hand the native agent its files without crossing into mounts
8: 
9: ## Context
10: 
11: [ADR 0026](0026-run-native-agents-as-an-unprivileged-user.md) has root hand
12: the agent user its workspace and home with `chown -R -h`.
13: 
14: The research admission probe hands over `/workspace`, and Claude's probe
15: bind-mounts its native binary read-only inside it, at
16: `/workspace/.agent-harness/claude/claude`. `chown -R` stopped on that mount
17: with `Read-only file system`, so the hand-over failed and every Claude
18: admission probe failed before reaching a provider (cohort attempt 7, #307).
19: Through a writable bind mount the same command would have succeeded and
20: changed the owner of the host's file.
21: 
22: ## Decision
23: 
24: The hand-over changes the owner of each root it is given and of everything
25: below it, but never crosses into a mount point below a root:
26: 
27: - **Mounts are skipped.** A mount point below a root, read-only or writable,
28:   is neither changed nor descended into. The hand-over reads the container's
29:   mount table (`/proc/self/mountinfo`) to find them.
30: - **Roots are always handed over**, even when a root is itself a mount point,
31:   such as a tmpfs `/workspace`.
32: - **Symlinks are changed, never followed**, including a root that is a
33:   symlink.
34: - **Failures say why.** A directory the hand-over cannot list fails it, and a
35:   failed hand-over's error carries the tail of its stderr.
36: - **The record keeps it.** The agent user record keeps the workspace
37:   hand-over's count of changed paths and the mounts it skipped, under
38:   `handover`.
39: 
40: The rest of ADR 0026 is unchanged.
41: 
42: ## Consequences
43: 
44: - Admission probes hand over a workspace that holds read-only runtime mounts.
45:   The mounted files keep their owner: the host's files are never changed, and
46:   the agent only executes them.
47: - The hand-over runs `python3` as root in the container, which creating the
48:   agent user already requires.

**No.** The 35 qualification outcomes do not justify ranking the seven arms or saying comparative Stage A is complete. They establish that a bounded **operational qualification** completed; they are not results from the comparative cohort. The README says this explicitly, though its “25-task” description is stale relative to the amended current contract. [README.md:8–11, 27–31](README.md)

### What the qualification establishes

Issue #180 recorded and audited **35/35 outcomes** across seven arms and five Python projects: 31 passes, three verifier failures, one eligible timeout, and no unresolved slots. The run involved 36 attempts because an original infrastructure-failed attempt was retained separately. It also spanned documented repair revisions. The final evidence says the solve rate was not the operational gate’s acceptance criterion, and these results “do not support a comparative ranking or numerical freeze.” [docs/evidence/current-qualification-180-final.md:3–15, 41–52](docs/evidence/current-qualification-180-final.md)

The qualification does provide evidence that the shared execution path—task preparation, candidate capture, cleanup/quiescence, independent verification, and result recording—worked for that five-project check. It does **not** qualify the MultiLang-specific parser and compiled-language resource requirements, or Stage B. [README.md:15–20](README.md); [docs/runbooks/current-qualification.md:28–30, 174–179](docs/runbooks/current-qualification.md)

The seven-arm pass counts might look sortable, but the README and final report explicitly classify them as operational evidence, not comparative results. They are five Python-project outcomes, not trials on the frozen Stage A corpus.

### What the current comparative cohort requires

There are two task counts to reconcile:

- The README’s “25-task” wording reflects the selected MultiLang corpus.
- The current v5 amendment screens the **23-task reviewed archive subset**: two of the 25 selected tasks were left unresolved and dropped without replacement. The effective schedule is **23 tasks × 7 standard arms × 1 attempt = 161 slots**, not 175. ADR-0016 explicitly supersedes the earlier 25-task/175-slot count; the v5 contract carries that amendment. [docs/authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md:10–15, 39–43, 108–123](docs/authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md); [docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md:13–20, 38–46](docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md)

- Stage A must run the full frozen schedule under one admitted configuration and owner-approved numerical freeze. The 23-task cohort advances through its blocks continuously; a non-clean block stops it. After every slot is terminal or explicitly unstarted, an offline audit precedes the seal. [docs/authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md:51–65, 83–89](docs/authoritative/adr/0016-screen-stage-a-on-23-reviewed-tasks.md); [docs/runbooks/stage-a-continuous-cohort.md:3–19, 21–42](docs/runbooks/stage-a-continuous-cohort.md)

- The freeze is more than a task list: v5 requires exact arm and runtime identities, corpus and verifier, policy, schedule, budgets/resources, window, admissions, outcome-slot plan, and owner approval. The v5 document is a prospective contract—not itself an actual numerical freeze or execution authorization. [docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md:3–10, 22–36](docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md)

Even a completed screening report is not a precise league table. It must report denominators, missingness, uncertainty and paired comparisons; one task is 1/23 of an arm’s denominator. The futility rule is an absolute near-total-failure threshold, not a relative ranking. [docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md:240–271, 348–373](docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md)

### What remains unverified

The retained comparative execution evidence does not show a completed 161-slot cohort, full audit, Stage A seal, or screening report. For example, attempt 6 stopped after 28 slots: 15 results (12 passes, three failures), 13 infrastructure-failed/unknown slots, and an interrupted in-flight slot. The ledger-transfer record says attempt 6 was retired before the move for attempt 7; ADR-0027 records that attempt 7’s Claude admission probes failed before reaching a provider. These are execution/recovery evidence, not a completed cohort. [docs/evidence/stage-a-cohort-attempt-6-20261008.md:9–28](docs/evidence/stage-a-cohort-attempt-6-20261008.md); [docs/evidence/research-ledger-transfer-cachyos-asrock-to-cachyos-alexander-20261009.md:3–6](docs/evidence/research-ledger-transfer-cachyos-asrock-to-cachyos-alexander-20261009.md); [docs/authoritative/adr/0027-hand-the-agent-its-files-without-crossing-into-mounts.md:14–18](docs/authoritative/adr/0027-hand-the-agent-its-files-without-crossing-into-mounts.md)

Accordingly, the cited evidence does **not** verify a seven-arm ranking, Stage A completion, futility dispositions or survivor set, or Stage B results. Stage B requires the sealed Stage A disposition and report, then a separately frozen cohort on new tasks; its results are not pooled with Stage A. [docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md:38–61, 273–298](docs/contracts/staged-multilang-benchmark-v5.md)

One more source of confusion: the September 2026 freeze publication describes an approved **historical 25-task numerical freeze**, but says the whole issue was not complete and that no comparative slot had run at that point. That approval cannot be read as evidence of a finished cohort, and it does not change the later 23-task amendment. [docs/evidence/stage-a-unsigned-review-50-20260920.md:14–38, 40–45](docs/evidence/stage-a-unsigned-review-50-20260920.md)

This was a read-only inspection; no files were changed.
